notes:
GLASS CLEANER DILUTION - READ FIRST. Briller Glass Cleaner (B508) is used DIRECT or diluted 1:1, per src/data/products.ts:446, which is the generator of record named in catalogue.json's own generatedFrom field. During this build catalogue.json was edited on disk to say Dilution=1:50 for briller-glass-cleaner, and the glass ad copy was edited to match it. Both were reverted here because products.ts still says Direct / 1:1 and the live product page renders from products.ts, so the ads would have contradicted their own landing page and told buyers to dilute a ready-to-use product 50x. catalogue.json itself was NOT edited by this agent - someone must reconcile it with products.ts, or re-run extract-catalogue.mjs, before this theme is imported. Note that assemble.mjs does not check dilutions, so nothing downstream would have caught this. Only 1:50 claim that is correct is Wash & Wax.

DILUTIONS ARE PER catalogue.json, NOT per the theme brief. The brief said 'Multipurpose is 1:5 and the others are 1:50'. The catalogue disagrees and the catalogue wins: Wash & Wax 1:50, Multipurpose Cleaner 1:5, Glass Cleaner direct or 1:1, Quick Dressing 1:1, Quick Tyre Shine no dilution stated. Ad copy states only those, and the Tyre Shine ads state no ratio at all. If the ratios change, these are the exact strings to update: 'Concentrate, Dilutes 1:50', 'Use Direct or Dilute 1:1', 'Dilutes 1:5 for Interiors', 'Dilutes 1:1 From 20 L' and their Arabic equivalents.

MADE IN CANADA IS BRILLER ONLY. The tyre ad group is the one place two brands share a landing page, so the copy says 'Briller tyre shine is made in Canada' rather than letting the claim attach to Smart Car Tyre Foam, whose origin is not in the catalogue. Do not edit that line into a generic one. The scoped 'Made in Canada' callout in assets.json attaches by campaign name containing 'wash care', which both campaign names do.

TYRE AD GROUP USES A FILTERED HUB URL: /b2c/products?category=tyre. Briller Quick Tyre Shine (20 L) and Smart Car Tyre Foam (650 ml) are two SKUs for one search intent, and the filtered catalogue page shows both. assemble.mjs validates the filter value against catalogue.categories and 'tyre' is a real category, and the existing hand-authored sitelinks already use this pattern. Click it once before launch anyway. Every other final URL is a literal url_b2c_* value from catalogue.json.

BID STRATEGY: 'Maximize conversions' is set for consistency with the other themes, but a brand-new account has no conversion data to maximise. Launch on Maximize clicks with the per-ad-group maxCpcQAR values here as the cap, and switch to Maximize conversions once WhatsApp-click conversions are tracked and running at roughly 15+ per month. The per-ad-group CPCs (QAR 1.80-2.50) are deliberately far below what the PPF and ceramic themes should pay; these are repeat consumables, not one-off high-ticket items.

TWO DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS FROM THE KEYWORD BRIEFS, both because sharedNegatives are expanded onto EVERY campaign in the whole account, including the sibling themes:
1. No bare 'near me' / 'بالقرب مني' negative. The briefs recommend it, but ABK has a walk-in shop, so 'car care products near me' is a good query. Only service-plus-near-me combinations are blocked.
2. No 'car detailing', 'window tinting', 'car tinting', 'ceramic coating', 'car wash', 'installation', 'تظليل سيارات' or 'تلميع سيارات' as bare phrase negatives. Each of those would destroy a sibling theme's best keywords: 'car detailing products qatar', 'window tinting film roll qatar', 'car wash chemicals supplier qatar', 'مواد تلميع سيارات', and 'ppf installation gel' which is a real catalogue product (autotriz-ppf-gel). Only unambiguous service constructions are blocked at account level. The tint, PPF, ceramic and polish theme owners should add the head-term service negatives at their own ad-group level, where they can see their own positives.

OTHER NEGATIVE-LIST TRAPS DELIBERATELY AVOIDED: bare 'service' would block the company's own name, ABK Trading & Service. Bare 'مركز' would block 'شامبو سيارات مركز' (concentrated), a core B2B query, because Google ignores Arabic diacritics and it collides with مركز (centre). Bare 'خدمة' appears in the Arabic company name. Bare 'free' would block 'streak free glass cleaner'. None of these appear in any list here.

GEO NEGATIVES ARE PER AD GROUP, NOT SHARED, for the same account-wide reason: a sibling GCC wholesale campaign will legitimately want Dubai and Riyadh traffic. Qatar-only location targeting does most of this work regardless.

AD SCHEDULE: the schedule string matches the house standard, but the real hours are 10:00-13:00 and 16:00-22:00 with Friday closed. Conversion here is a human replying on WhatsApp, so consider a bid-down on the 13:00-16:00 gap rather than paying full price for leads nobody answers for three hours.

ARABIC NEEDS A NATIVE-SPEAKER PASS before launch, same as the rest of the site's Arabic. It is MSA, tashkeel stripped so no character is wasted on a shadda, Western digits only, no em-dash or terminal punctuation, and no headline starts with a Latin token or a digit, all per the RTL rules. Preview every Arabic asset in Google's own ad preview, not a code editor. Keywords intentionally carry the Gulf colloquial forms (كفرات, طبلون) and hamza-less spellings (اطارات, اغراض) while the ad copy stays MSA (إطارات, الأغراض); that split is intentional, not an inconsistency.

NO SERVICE PROMISE ANYWHERE. Every CTA is 'ask on WhatsApp for a quote' or 'walk in to the Doha shop'. No price, discount or 'from QAR' language appears, and none should be added, since the site publishes no prices.
